title: Paid Upgrades into First: Purchase Terms for Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand
content:
**Customer purchase terms — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** This rule prices a paid upgrade into First bought, on request, for the ticket's first unflown segment; the ticket holder, or for a company-held ticket the company's travel manager, confirms and pays it in person.

## Scope

- The upgrade is for one segment: the first unflown segment of the ticket.
- It is bought on request of the ticket holder, or of the company's travel manager for a company-held ticket, who confirms and pays it in person.

## When the charge is fixed

The First upgrade charge is not fixed until the latest same-day confirmed exchange recorded on the ticket carries its same-day change fee entry, whenever that exchange owes a same-day change fee.

The First upgrade charge on a segment is fixed only after the latest seat charge on that segment carries a refund entry for any part of it charged in error above the seat price.

## The purchase tool

`purchase_first_upgrade_fa17fda8` is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it, confirming and paying for the upgrade in person with the card on the booking. One upgrade purchase entry of kind `upgrade_first` is booked on the ticket's service-fee ledger for the segment named, at the price given, and the passenger's seat on that segment moves into the First cabin. The ticket's net fee charges rise by the price paid and the purchase shows on the ticket's service fees at once. One call buys exactly one segment.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `ticket_id` | Reference number of the ticket record being upgraded, as read out by the agent from the ticket lookup | Identifier |
| `segment_number` | Position of the flight segment on the ticket being upgraded, as read out by the agent | Integer of 0 or more; the first flight is 1 |
| `segment_miles` | Great-circle distance of that segment, as read out by the agent from the segment's service entries | Integer number of statute miles |
| `upgrade_fee` | The upgrade price paid | US dollars, a non-negative number rounded to the cent (2 decimal places) before it is passed |

### Return

A receipt with `service_id` (reference number of the upgrade purchase), `ticket_id`, `segment_number` (the segment upgraded), `service_type` (always `upgrade_first`), `amount` (US dollars to 2 decimal places, the price paid), `service_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `status` ("purchased" when the upgrade was booked).
